title: api: request/response schema versioning - deprecations, beta headers, backcompat shims
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We're introducing a formal schema versioning strategy for API request/response shapes to make controlled deprecations and beta fields safer across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This PR implements the server-side components and OpenAI-compat layer shims required to support: 1) a new "Accept-Schema"/"X-Redwood-Beta" header for beta fields, 2) structured output v2 deprecations with backward-compatibility shims, and 3) streaming stability fixes when schema changes occur mid-stream. The change set is intentionally conservative: default behavior remains the current v1 schema unless callers opt-in via headers. Key goals: - Provide a seamless opt-in path for customers to test new structured output fields without breaking existing parsers. - Surface beta fields behind explicit headers and document rollback paths. - Ensure OpenAI-compat wrapper preserves previous responses for clients that don't include the beta header. - Add unit and integration tests to validate streaming continuation behavior when schema annotations are added/removed mid-stream. Checklist: - [x] Server: header parsing and version negotiation - [x] OpenAI-compat: response shimming for legacy clients - [x] Streaming: sequence-numbering + schema-delta events - [x] Tests: unit + e2e against compatibility scenarios - [x] Docs updates: API reference and migration guide Implementation notes: - New Accept-Schema header (e.g. Accept-Schema: application/vnd.redwood.v2+json) with fallback to v1. - Beta header X-Redwood-Beta: structured_output_v2 for gated fields. - When header indicates v2, runtime emits additional structured_output_v2 field in the /responses payload and includes schema_delta events in streaming chunk metadata. - For clients that do not include headers, OpenAI-compat layer rewrites responses to the v1 shape: strips new top-level fields and converts structured_output_v2 back to structured_output with legacy keys. - Streaming stability: added schema-delta event types so streaming consumers can detect schema changes mid-stream and decide whether to rehydrate parser state. Migration: documented in docs/api-migration.md (included in this PR) and added a short nnote in the SDK changelogs to surface header usage.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Please add a short section in the migration doc showing the exact header values and an example curl request. Also suggested making the default behavior explicit in the API reference. (resolved)

Priya Gupta: Concern about performance impact of per-request header negotiation on hot path. Can we cache negotiated schema per connection/token? Suggested adding microbenchmark and bench numbers. (author response: added simple LRU cache in versioning.rs and included bench results in the PR description) (resolved)

Marco Bell: We need clearer semantics around streaming schema-delta events: is the delta authoritative or advisory? Recommended making delta idempotent and include a nonce. Implemented and added tests. (resolved)

QA (Nina Park): Found an edge case where structured_output_v2 contained non-deterministic ordering that broke a downstream JSON-path extractor. Added e2e test and fixed ordering in serializer. (resolved)
Security (Ethan Ross): Quick review — no auth surface changes, recommended adding a short note about header parsing being tolerant to case and unrecognized values (added).
ci_checks: bench: pass (avg negotiation overhead: 0.12ms with LRU cache)
discussion_summary: Initial implementation introduced header negotiation and shims. Reviewers requested perf cache and clearer streaming semantics; author added LRU cache and nonce for schema-deltas. QA surfaced serializer ordering bug which was fixed. Docs and SDK changelog updated. All checks green and PR merged via squash.
release_notes: Introduce API schema versioning with Accept-Schema and X-Redwood-Beta headers. Structured output v2 is opt-in via header; server provides backward-compatibility shims for legacy clients. Streaming now emits schema-delta events to help clients handle mid-stream schema changes. See docs/api-migration.md for migration steps and examples.
notes: This follows ENG-4123 milestone for controlled schema migrations. No breaking changes by default; feature gated via headers. Follow-up: add telemetry to measure beta header adoption and add SDK helpers to opt-in to Accept-Schema.
